hypotheses.justification: `hι` follows from `hB` together with the field `P₁.perfect : Function.Bijective P₁.B` in `LevelPairing` (Definitions/Def_HeckeModule_IharaRungDatum.lean). Suppose `ι x = ι y`. For every `z`, `hB` gives `P₁.B x z = Pₐ.B (ι x) (ι z) = Pₐ.B (ι y) (ι z) = P₁.B y z`. So `P₁.B x = P₁.B y` by `LinearMap.ext`, and `P₁.perfect.1` (injectivity of `P₁.B`) gives `x = y`. To remove the hypothesis, add one line at the start of the proof: `have hι : Function.Injective ι := fun x y hxy => P₁.perfect.1 (LinearMap.ext fun z => by rw [hB, hB, hxy])`. The rest of the proof stays as written: `LinearEquiv.ofInjective ι hι` and so on. No degenerate case causes trouble, because the derivation is purely algebraic and holds for any types and rings.
